jamie_support: FYI — Customer 'MaplePay' (enterprise) reporting repeated 502/504s to hosted inference since ~09:10 UTC. Ticket INC-5409. They see 'TLS handshake timeout' in our gateway logs. Pasting a short excerpt from edge-pop-3 logs:

jamie_support: ```
2026-03-17T09:11:14Z edge-pop-3 gw[conn-45123] INFO: upstream=203.0.113.45:443 tcp_established=1 tls_handshake_start=2026-03-17T09:11:14Z tls_handshake_timeout=2026-03-17T09:11:29Z result=handshake_timeout
2026-03-17T09:11:15Z edge-pop-3 gw[conn-45124] INFO: upstream=203.0.113.46:443 tcp_established=1 tls_alert=unexpected_message result=handshake_error
```

jamie_support: Cert rotation job `cert-rotation/v2026.03` started ~09:00 and was canaryed to edge-pop-1/2/3. Customer saw spike after pop-3 roll.

ben_sre: Can you repro from the same VPC/region? Ask them to run a quick `curl -v` to our hosted endpoint and paste output. Also need `dig +trace` for their resolver and whether they're using EDNS0.

jamie_support: Customer ran `curl -v` from their app host (us-east-1):

jamie_support: ```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/infer -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>'
* Connected to api.redwood.example.com (203.0.113.45) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLS handshake has timed out
* Closing connection 0
curl: (28) Operation timed out after 30001 milliseconds with 0 bytes received
```

carmen_eng: Two hypotheses: 1) the new cert chain has an intermediate that's triggering a resolver/OCSP TCP fetch which is timing out on some network paths (EDNS0 UDP->TCP fallback), or 2) TLS session resumption behavior changed and broke an upstream load balancer that expects resumed sessions. Both can surface as "handshake timeout" if TCP establishes but TLS stalls.

carmen_eng: Can you get `dig +short @8.8.8.8 maplepay.example.com` and `dig +dnssec @their-resolver maplepay.example.com` and also `curl --resolve` from a public jump? Example command I want you to try from an external host:

carmen_eng: ```
curl -v --resolve api.redwood.example.com:443:203.0.113.45 https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/health
```

jamie_support: Ran the exact `--resolve` from an EC2 in same AZ, output below:

jamie_support: ```
*   Trying 203.0.113.45:443...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to api.redwood.example.com (203.0.113.45) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering http/1.1
* TLS 1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLS handshake has timed out
* Closing connection 0
curl: (28) Operation timed out after 10001 milliseconds with 0 bytes received
```

ben_sre: Please also attach a traceroute using TCP to 443 so we can see where packet loss or non-responsiveness occurs: `traceroute -T -p 443 203.0.113.45`.

jamie_support: Traceroute (from customer app host):

jamie_support: ```
traceroute to 203.0.113.45 (203.0.113.45), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.0.1  0.3 ms  0.2 ms  0.2 ms
 2  198.51.100.21  1.1 ms  1.0 ms  1.0 ms
 3  * * *
 4  203.0.113.45  18.9 ms  18.8 ms  18.7 ms
```

jamie_support: Note: TCP connects succeed (we see tcp_established in logs) but TLS step stalls.

carmen_eng: That pattern fits ECN/PMTU or UDP->TCP fallback behavior: if a resolver reply gets truncated (EDNS0) and the client's resolver falls back to TCP, some firewalls or middleboxes drop large DNS-over-TCP responses or block outbound TCP to port 53, delaying A/AAAA resolution and causing downstream TLS handshakes to stall. Also possible: OCSP stapling failure if our CA's OCSP responder needs a TCP fetch.

carmen_eng: Quick mitigation options:
- Roll back cert-rotation on the affected pop (edge-pop-3) to previous chain (v2026.02)
- Add temporary per-pop fallback routing to pop-1/pop-2 for MaplePay
- Increase TLS handshake timeout on edge-pop-3 for TCP established -> TLS complete path while we investigate

jamie_support: I'm initiating a rollback for edge-pop-3. Tagging ops.

deploy-bot: ```
[deploy-bot] 09:14:02 UTC: Initiating canary rollback cert-rotation v2026.03 -> v2026.02 on edge-pop-3 (requested by jamie_support).
[deploy-bot] 09:14:22 UTC: Rollback completed on edge-pop-3. Health checks OK.
```

jamie_support: Customer reports error rate falling back to baseline within ~30s after rollback. They confirm MaplePay can send inferences again.

dave_sales: Drafting customer note: "We identified an issue during a cert chain rollout that caused TLS handshakes to stall on a subset of network paths. We rolled back the cert on the affected POP and traffic has recovered. We're investigating root cause and will follow up with mitigations. Apologies for the outage."

ben_sre: Follow-ups for the eng team:
- Capture full pcap on a reproducer host showing TCP establish + TLS ClientHello but no ServerHello (to confirm OCSP/DNS-TCP stall).
- Add resolver TCP health checks and metrics (time to complete A/AAAA over UDP vs TCP) to Console observability.
- Consider short-term increase of handshake timeout for TCP-fallback paths and add canary gating for cert chain changes that affect OCSP chains.

ben_sre: Closing the support thread for INC-5409 — mitigation succeeded (rollback). Opening ENG-1427 to track investigation and long-term fixes.
